subject: Model fit & capacity snapshot for onboarding — next steps
messages:

Subject: Model fit & capacity snapshot for onboarding — next steps

Hi Nora,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday — this thread captures a concise model shortlist and an initial capacity snapshot so your engineering team can scope the integration work. I attached the workbook with model profiles and a CSV with the token-volume scenarios. High-level recommendations below:

- Model shortlist (recommended order):
  1) Mistral-Instruct-XL (8B) — good latency/cost mix for moderate context (up to 4k) and structured completion tasks.
  2) LLaMA-2-Chat-70B (8k) — best quality for complex dialog and long instructions; higher GPU memory / quantization work required.
  3) Falcon-40B-Instruct (16k) — fallback when higher context is needed and for batch-heavy reranking flows.

- Context needs: core QA flow assumed 3–4k tokens. Long-document summarization (customer use-case) will need up to 12k for the rare long-job path — recommend server-side chunking + stitching.

- Token volume (projections):
  * Day-1 pilot: 150k tokens/day (mostly inference for short QA).
  * Month-3 typical: 1.2M tokens/day (50–70 concurrent sessions peak hour).
  * Peak flash: 3.5M tokens/day (events driven) — needs autoscale / burst plan.

- Serving recommendations:
  * Use quantized Mistral-XL for baseline to hit latency SLOs; reserve 1-2 nodes of LLaMA-2-Chat for quality-sensitive routes.
  * Batching: 50–150 ms target queuing; prefer micro-batching for chat paths and larger batches for background summarization.

Next steps I suggest: engineering sync to finalize peak concurrency assumptions (Vivek + your eng lead), pick a pilot model variant and confirm inference SLA targets, and schedule a short ops walkthrough for token instrumentation.

Attachments: model_profiles.xlsx (per-model perf/ram/quantization notes), token_estimates.csv (scenario breakdown).

Thanks,
Monica

On Wed, Aug 6, 2025 at 08:34 AM Nora Patel <nora.patel@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks Monica — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
> 1) The 12k context path will come from our ingest pipeline for long reports; those jobs will be queued and can tolerate longer latency (30–45s). Does Redwood recommend chunk-and-stitch or a long-context model for that lane?

Hi Nora — good question. Our recommendation: start with chunk-and-stitch to reduce engineering risk and cost. We can support a long-context model later if stitching introduces unacceptable coherence issues. Operationally:

- Chunk-and-stitch approach:
  * Pre-split documents into ~2–3k token chunks.
  * Run a short instruction pass per chunk and then a second pass to synthesize summaries.
  * Pros: predictable memory usage, easier to scale horizontally.
  * Cons: possible minor coherence loss on edge cases; we should include a small eval set to validate.

- Long-context model option:
  * LLaMA-2-Chat-70B (8k) is our immediate step; for 12k you’d need Falcon-40B-Long or a 16k variant and heavier infra; this requires additional quantization work and run-time tuning.

Vivek, Jordan, Soojin — can you confirm ops checklist items for a quantized LLaMA-2 rollout and whether we have existing playbooks for chunking pipelines? I can host a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the workbook.

I’ve attached a short plan (poa_workplan.pdf) with proposed owners and timeline: pilot (2 weeks), validation (2 weeks), production ramp (4–6 weeks).

Thanks,
Monica

Quick ops confirm:

- Quantized LLaMA-2-Chat (4-bit QAT/C4 path) — we have a validated build that hits ~220ms p95 on our 1xA100 profile for 4k contexts; it will require ~60 GB of GPU to run reliably for production per instance.
- For the chunk-and-stitch flow we recommend a worker pool sized to handle peak chunk concurrency: roughly 12 workers for the 50–70 peak concurrent sessions Nora mentioned. That maps to the token volumes Monica listed (1.2–1.7M/day) with a safety buffer.
